name: San José
authority: City of San José Environmental Services Department (SanJoseRecycles.org)
notes: San José single-family homes have no food-scraps cart: garbage goes to a materials recovery facility that pulls out organics for composting. Yard trimmings have their own cart or street pile.

cardboard_box.reason: Cut boxes small enough to fit loosely in the cart.
cardboard_box.quote: Cut large boxes small enough to fit loosely inside the recycling cart.

pizza_box_greasy.reason: Greasy boxes go in garbage; recycle clean lids.
pizza_box_greasy.quote: Put boxes stained with grease or oil in the garbage.

paper_mixed.reason: Recycle clean paper; no foil, grease or food residue.
paper_mixed.quote: Recycle clean paper. Tape is OK.

paperboard_box.reason: Recycle clean boxes; liners and soiled parts don't go in.

paper_bag.reason: Recycle clean paper bags; glued-on handles are OK.
paper_bag.quote: Paper bags can be recycled even if they have handles attached with adhesive.

shredded_paper.reason: Put shreds in a clear bag, tie it, then recycle.
shredded_paper.quote: To prevent shredded paper from getting tangled in recycling equipment, place it in a clear bag.

paper_towel_napkin.reason: Garbage cart; San José sorts out soiled paper for composting.
paper_towel_napkin.quote: Soiled paper that you put in your garbage cart will be separated out at the “Materials Recovery Facility” and sent to a composting facility in Gilroy.

tissue.reason: Used tissues go in the garbage; never flush them.
tissue.quote: Tissues and Toilet Paper Put in Garbage Cart/Bin

paper_cup.reason: Plastic-lined cups go in garbage; recycle the cardboard sleeve.
paper_cup.quote: Paper Cups Put in Garbage Cart/Bin

paper_plate_used.reason: Garbage cart; San José sorts out soiled paper for composting.
paper_plate_used.quote: Soiled paper that you put in your garbage cart will be separated out at the “Materials Recovery Facility” and sent to a composting facility in Gilroy.

paper_takeout.reason: Food-soiled take-out boxes go in the garbage.
paper_takeout.quote: Food and Liquid Soiled Containers Belong in the Garbage.

carton.reason: Empty cartons, then recycle; caps go in the garbage.
carton.quote: Empty the cartons of any liquid or residue and, if possible, remove any plastic or metal caps or spouts before recycling.

aseptic_carton.reason: Juice boxes go in recycling; straws go in garbage.
aseptic_carton.quote: Please place them in your recycling container.

receipt.reason: Receipts contain BPA and can't be recycled; garbage.
receipt.quote: Paper Receipts Put in Garbage Cart/Bin

coffee_grounds_filter.reason: Coffee grounds and paper filters go in the garbage cart.
coffee_grounds_filter.quote: Coffee Filters Put in Garbage Cart/Bin

tea_bag.reason: Tea bags can contain plastic; put them in the garbage.
tea_bag.quote: Tea bags can contain plastic and are therefore trash.

book.reason: Recycle books; donate ones in good condition.

plastic_bottle.reason: Empty plastic bottles, then recycle; no rinsing needed.
plastic_bottle.quote: Empty out plastic bottles before recycling.

plastic_jug.reason: Empty jugs, no rinse needed; caps can stay on.
plastic_jug.quote: Empty jugs before placing in the recycling cart (no need to rinse).

plastic_tub.reason: Empty and scrape tubs, then recycle.
plastic_tub.quote: Before recycling, empty and scrape out any food residue left in the cups.

plastic_clamshell.reason: Recycle if marked #1-#5 or #7; unmarked, #6 or compostable: garbage.
plastic_clamshell.quote: In San José, you can recycle hard plastic packaging labeled #1 – #5 in the ‘chasing arrow’ symbol.

plastic_cup.reason: Recycle empty cups marked #1-#5 or #7; #6 or compostable: garbage.
plastic_cup.quote: Recycle plastic cups only if they are empty and labeled plastic #1 through 5 or non-compostable plastic #7.

plastic_takeout.reason: Empty and scrape, then recycle; not if compostable plastic.
plastic_takeout.quote: Before recycling, empty and scrape the food residue out of the container.

plastic_bag.reason: Not curbside recyclable; garbage, or clean bags to store drop-off.
plastic_bag.quote: While plastic bags cannot be recycled in your curbside recycling container, you can use this site to find local places that will take them.

bubble_wrap.reason: Take clean wrap to a plastic bag drop-off; otherwise garbage.
bubble_wrap.quote: If you are unable to take bubble wrap to a plastic bag drop-off location or your local mail center, place them in the garbage.

plastic_utensils.reason: Too small to recycle; plastic utensils go in garbage.
plastic_utensils.quote: They will fall through cracks in sorting machinery. Toss them in the garbage.

snack_wrapper.reason: Mixed-material bags can't be recycled; garbage.
snack_wrapper.quote: these mixed-material bags cannot be recycled. Toss them in the garbage.

compostable_plastic.reason: "Compostable" plastics must go in the garbage.
compostable_plastic.quote: Plastic items labeled “compostable” or “biodegradable” must go in the garbage.

foam_food_container.reason: Foam containers aren't recyclable here, even clean.
foam_food_container.quote: Takeout Containers (Foam) Put in Garbage Cart/Bin

foam_packaging.reason: Bag packing peanuts, tie shut, put in garbage.
foam_packaging.quote: Place packing peanuts in a clear plastic bag and tie shut, then toss in your garbage cart.

plastic_cap.reason: Loose caps: garbage. Caps screwed onto bottles can be recycled.
plastic_cap.quote: Loose plastic caps should go in the garbage.

coffee_pod.reason: Pods are too small to recycle curbside; garbage.
coffee_pod.quote: Coffee Pods & Capsules Put in Garbage Cart/Bin

drink_pouch.reason: Drink pouches go in the garbage.
drink_pouch.quote: Drink Pouches Put in Garbage Cart/Bin

toothpaste_tube.reason: Toothpaste tubes go in the garbage.
toothpaste_tube.quote: Toothpaste Tubes Put in Garbage Cart/Bin

toothbrush.reason: Manual toothbrushes: garbage. Electric ones are e-waste.

plastic_toy.reason: Recycle hard plastic toys; ones with electronics are e-waste.
plastic_toy.quote: Plastic Toys Put in Recycling Cart/Bin

aluminum_can.quote: Aluminum Cans Put in Recycling Cart/Bin

food_can.reason: Empty and scrape cans; labels can stay on.
food_can.quote: Empty and scrape cans before recycling.

aluminum_foil.reason: Clean foil only; roll into a ball at least 2 inches wide.
aluminum_foil.quote: Scrape residue off all aluminum foil before recycling.

aluminum_tray.reason: Empty and scrape trays; traces of food are OK.
aluminum_tray.quote: Empty and scrape all containers before recycling.

aerosol_can.reason: Hazardous waste unless completely empty; empty cans go in recycling.
aerosol_can.quote: Only empty aerosol cans are allowed in the recycling cart.

glass_bottle.reason: Empty, remove caps, then recycle; blue glass is not accepted.
glass_bottle.quote: Empty glass bottles of any liquid or residue and remove any plastic or metal caps before recycling.

glass_jar.reason: Scrape jars empty and take off lids, then recycle.
glass_jar.quote: Scrape out any leftover food or drink before recycling empty glass jars.

broken_glass.reason: Bottle and jar shards only; other broken glass: wrap, garbage.
broken_glass.quote: Recycle ONLY broken bottles and jars.

drinking_glass.note: SanJoseRecycles contradicts itself: the glassware page says a regular drinking glass can go in the blue recycling cart, but the broken-glass page says 'other drink glasses ... cannot be recycled' and the dishes page says glass dishes cannot go in recycling.

ceramic.reason: Ceramic dishes go in the garbage.
ceramic.quote: Put a small amount (less than 60 pounds) in the garbage.

food_scraps.reason: Garbage cart; San José recovers food from garbage for composting.
food_scraps.quote: All the garbage collected in San José is sent to a mixed waste materials recovery facility (MRF) to recover organic materials for composting.

bones.reason: Bones go in the garbage cart.

yard_trimmings.reason: Yard trimmings cart or pile; keep produce and dog poop bags out.
yard_trimmings.quote: Accepted yard trimmings include branches, prunings and clippings (e.g. flowers, grass, leaves, palm fronds), and sod (remove as much soil as possible).

flowers.reason: Flowers go with yard trimmings; remove packaging first.

cooking_oil.reason: Up to 1 quart: cool, seal in can or jar, garbage. More: hazardous.
cooking_oil.quote: Let cool, then put small quantities in cans or jars. Seal containers and put in the garbage.

wooden_chopsticks.reason: Garbage cart; wooden chopsticks are sorted out and composted.
wooden_chopsticks.quote: Wooden chopsticks are separated out from garbage and composted.

battery.reason: Banned from carts; take to County household hazardous waste.
battery.quote: All batteries, including sizes AAA, AA, C, and D, need to be disposed of as Household Hazardous Waste.

phone_electronics.reason: E-waste: County Household Hazardous Waste Program; never in carts.
phone_electronics.quote: Cell phones are e-waste that can be disposed of through the County Household Hazardous Waste Program.

cords_cables.reason: E-waste: County Household Hazardous Waste Program.
cords_cables.quote: Electrical cords and cables are e-waste that can be disposed of through the County Household Hazardous Waste Program.

bulb_fluorescent.reason: Hazardous waste: County HHW program or a mail-back kit.
bulb_fluorescent.quote: Both fluorescent light bulbs and tubes can be disposed of through the County Household Hazardous Waste Program.

bulb_led.reason: LEDs contain lead and arsenic; dispose as hazardous waste.
bulb_led.quote: Store them in a sealed container, and dispose of them as hazardous waste.

bulb_incandescent.reason: Wrap and put in garbage; don't recycle with glass.
bulb_incandescent.quote: The materials used to make incandescent bulbs are non-toxic, so it’s OK to throw these bulbs in the garbage.

paint.reason: Hazardous waste, free County drop-off; dried latex can go in garbage.
paint.quote: All other paint, including spray paint, is hazardous waste and can be disposed of for free through the County Household Hazardous Waste Program.

cleaning_product.reason: Leftover cleaners are hazardous waste; empty bottles are often recyclable.

medicine.reason: Never trash or flush; use a drop-off bin, hhw.org or mailback.
medicine.quote: As for the medicines themselves, do not flush unused or expired medicines down the toilet, the drain, or put them in the garbage or recycling carts.

sharps.reason: Seal in a biohazard container; County HHW or drop-off site.
sharps.quote: Needles and sharps must be placed in a biohazard container for disposal with other hazardous waste.

propane_cylinder.reason: Never in carts, fire risk; County hazardous waste drop-off.
propane_cylinder.quote: Never dispose of these cylinders in garbage or recycling carts as they can cause fires.

diaper.reason: Bag disposable diapers, then put in the garbage.
diaper.quote: Disposable diapers must be bagged before placing them in the garbage cart.

pet_waste.reason: Bag animal waste, then garbage; not with yard trimmings.
pet_waste.quote: Bag all animal waste before tossing it in your garbage cart.

kitty_litter.reason: Bag cat litter, then put in the garbage.
kitty_litter.quote: Bag kitty litter before tossing in the garbage.

face_mask.reason: Masks go in the garbage; snip the straps.
face_mask.quote: Face Masks Alternative ways to recycle Put in Garbage Cart/Bin

disposable_gloves.reason: Disposable gloves go in the garbage.
disposable_gloves.quote: Latex Gloves Put in Garbage Cart/Bin

textiles.quote: Clothing and Textiles Put in Garbage Cart/Bin

shoes.reason: Donate usable shoes; otherwise garbage. Light-up shoes are hazardous.
shoes.quote: Put in Garbage Cart/Bin If your shoes are in good condition, consider donating them.

cigarette.reason: Cigarette butts go in the garbage.
cigarette.quote: Cigarettes and butts are neither recyclable nor compostable.

wipes.reason: Wipes go in the garbage; never flush them.

garden_hose.reason: Hoses jam recycling equipment; always garbage.
garden_hose.quote: Never put hoses in the recycling — always put them in the garbage.

egg_carton_paper.reason: Only clean, dry paper egg cartons go in recycling.
egg_carton_paper.quote: Only clean, dry egg cartons can be put in recycling.

egg_carton_foam.reason: Foam (#6) egg cartons go in the garbage.
egg_carton_foam.quote: Egg Cartons (Foam) Put in Garbage Cart/Bin

frozen_food_box.reason: Recycle if no food residue; otherwise garbage.
frozen_food_box.quote: If there is no food residue on the box, place it in the recycling.

food_in_container.reason: Scrape the food into the garbage cart first, then scan the empty container.
food_in_container.quote: All the garbage collected in San José is sent to a mixed waste materials recovery facility (MRF) to recover organic materials for composting.

also.quote: Before recycling, empty and scrape the food residue out of the container.
